subject: MSA redlines — seat fallbacks, break-glass (governing law & injunctive relief)
messages:

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team has circulated a redline to your MSA focusing on governing law, arbitration, and the scope for equitable relief. Please find the redline attached (Meridian_MSA_redline_20250825.docx).

Two quick asks from our side:
- Governing law: Meridian is asking for New York law (we can discuss why on the call).
- Emergency relief: we need a clear pathway to obtain preliminary injunctive relief in state or federal court where Meridian operates — we can't be forced to wait for an arbitrator in time-critical cases.

Can you confirm Redwood's initial positions and who to loop in for a short redline call this week? We may also have external counsel hopping on.

Subject: Re: MSA redlines attached — governing law & urgent-relief carve

Emma — thanks for sending this over and for the clear callouts. I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (AM) to get aligned quickly.

High-level Redwood positions:
- Governing law: Redwood prefers Delaware or California for predictability. We understand Meridian's preference for NY and are open to discussing a compromise.
- Arbitration: Redwood generally wants arbitration for final dispute resolution (to control costs and predictability).
- Injunctive relief: we can accept a narrow carveout allowing either party to seek preliminary injunctive or other emergency equitable relief in court to preserve rights ("break-glass"), provided doing so doesn't waive arbitration for the merits.

Proposed next steps:
1) Short call (30m) to align on law/seat and the exact wording of the carveout — are you available Wed 8/27 10am PT?
2) Laura will propose suggested clause language and a small venue matrix showing trade-offs (we'll attach).
3) If we land on one of the options, we'll update the redline and circulate for final sign-off.

Cc: Olga from Legal Ops to confirm evidence-preservation ask and DocuSign readiness.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@meridianhealth.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Aug 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines attached — governing law & urgent-relief carve

Emma / team — following up with suggested language and rationale. I've attached a short venue matrix (Redwood_Venue_Matrix_20250825.xlsx). Key points and proposed redlines below: 

1) Governing law vs. seat: those are distinct. You can pick NY law with an arbitration seat elsewhere; that is a reasonable compromise in many deals.

2) Proposed injunctive relief carve (suggested wording):
"Notwithstanding the arbitration provisions in Section X, either party may seek interim or emergency equitable relief (including injunctive relief, temporary restraining orders, or other provisional remedies) in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo pending resolution of the dispute; seeking such relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the right to arbitrate the dispute on the merits. The parties shall promptly notify the arbitrator of any such filing and the arbitrator may consider such measures in any subsequent proceedings."

3) Service / consent / preservation: add a short clause for consent to service of process for emergency filings and mutual obligations to preserve logs, memory, and snapshots for 30 days after notice.

4) Seat recommendation: if Meridian insists on NY law, Redwood proposes arbitration seat be Delaware (or neutral ARB seat) — Delaware offers corporate law predictability and well-established procedure for enforcement of awards. If Meridian requires seat = NY, we can accept for revenue significance but will flag for leadership.

I'll attach a redlined excerpt in the next email. If this direction is acceptable, Karthik and Vivek can approve commercial concessions and we will issue a clean order form for signature.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Venue_Matrix_20250825.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@meridianhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: j.singh@dlapiper.com
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines attached — governing law & urgent-relief carve

Laura/Vivek — thanks for the clear proposals and the matrix. Meridian's position follows: 
- Governing law: Meridian must have New York law; it is non-negotiable internally due to procurement rules.
- Injunctive relief carve: we accept the wording you proposed but want it limited to "preliminary or emergency equitable relief" and include an explicit limit that the court relief is "temporary and without prejudice to the arbitration on the merits."
- Preservation: Meridian's counsel asks for a 60-day preservation window (logs, KV cache snapshots, and request metadata) in any emergency filing, not 30.

If Redwood accepts New York law with the carveout language (with our 60-day preservation), we can proceed to sign the order form next week. We agree that arbitration can be the forum for merits but require the ability to get emergency court relief quickly.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept NY law + 60-day preservation? Also please provide the emergency contact and a draft DocuSign link so we can keep momentum.

Best,
Emma Brooks
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Meridian Health
[Attachment: Meridian_Internal_Checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2025 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines attached — governing law & urgent-relief carve

Emma — appreciate the clarity and the willingness to move forward. Redwood's commercial position (approved by leadership for this deal):

1) Governing law: Redwood will accept New York governing law for Meridian Health given strategic value of the account.

2) Arbitration and seat: the parties will keep final-dispute arbitration, with the arbitration agreement to be governed by NY law but with the seat of arbitration to be set as Delaware unless Meridian insists on NYC seat. If Meridian requires seat = NYC, Redwood will accept but will record that as a material concession.

3) Injunctive relief carve: Redwood accepts Laura's proposed injunctive-carve language with Meridian's requested clarifying language that any such court-ordered relief is preliminary and without prejudice to arbitration on the merits.

4) Preservation window: Redwood agrees to a 60-day preservation obligation for emergency filings (logs, relevant KV cache snapshots, request/response metadata) scoped to the specific request and subject to Redwood's retention policies — Laura will draft narrow preservation language to avoid open-ended obligations.

5) Next steps: Olga will prepare the updated redline and a DocuSign order form. Can Meridian confirm preferred arbitration seat (Delaware or NYC) by EOD tomorrow? Once agreed, we'll route the final MSA + Order Form for signature and spin up the onboarding SOW.

Thanks — excited to get Meridian onboarded.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_Meridian_20250828.pdf (pdf)]
